name: Cross-Faction Tradeoff Matrix
rationale: Two rounds of small, high-diversity cross-faction breakouts maximize cross-faction exposure (31/38 pairs) and pair opposing stances on concrete negotiables (`evals_liability` and `benefit_sharing`). Ordering `labor_advocate` and `global_south_cso` first in the closing plenary and structuring the synthesis prompt around a 4-pillar package deal ensures civil society, open-weights, academia, industry, and sovereign governments all see their core red lines integrated into the final multi-faction agreement.

blocks.title: Pre-Deployment Evaluations & Liability Tradeoffs
blocks.prompt: Each participant has equal speaking time in a structured round-robin. Negotiate a concrete tradeoff package on pre-deployment evaluations and developer liability: Under what exact conditions can industry offer pre-deployment model access, incident reporting, and open evaluation tooling in exchange for targeted regulatory predictability, while guaranteeing binding red lines against CBRN/autonomous replication, workplace surveillance, and ethics dumping in the Global South?

blocks.title: Benefit Sharing, Compute Access & Open Innovation
blocks.prompt: Structured turn-taking: ensure every voice shapes the room's agreement. How do we balance frontier compute security and catastrophic risk thresholds (e.g., >10^26 FLOPs) with open-weight innovation, Global South compute capacity-building, and mandatory employer-funded worker transition and creative-consent frameworks? Identify specific concessions each side will make.

blocks.title: Closing Synthesis: The Multi-Pillar Accord
blocks.prompt: The Chair will call on each of the 10 delegates in turn for equal airtime—starting with Civil Society and Academia (`labor_advocate`, `global_south_cso`, `safety_researcher`), then Industry (`open_weights_lead`, `big_tech_policy`, `frontier_lab_ceo`), then Governments and Regulators (`uk_aisi`, `china_policy`, `us_natsec`, `eu_regulator`). We are drafting a single, unified 4-pillar Summit Accord that all 5 factions can endorse: (1) Sovereign coordination of national AI Safety Institutes on empirical pre-deployment CBRN/cyber/autonomy evals and incident hotlines; (2) Open-source safety evaluation benchmarks protecting responsible open-weight distribution below extreme capability red lines; (3) Binding prohibitions on Global South ethics dumping paired with regional public compute & capacity sharing; and (4) Mandatory workforce transition pipelines, creative consent/residuals, and bans on covert workplace biometric surveillance. State your concrete reciprocal commitment to adopt this unified package.
